extracted.intended_audience: researchers and administrators interested in NIH grant funding and workforce policy (early career investigators, institutional research administrators, policy analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and definitional guidance about Early Stage Investigators (ESIs) and related career-stage categories for R01-equivalent applications and awards, plus person-based metrics (discussion and funding rates) and policy actions affecting ESI support in FYs 2024–2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ESIs are those who are within 10 years of their terminal degree or completion of clinical training and who have not yet been awarded a substantial NIH grant (R01-equivalent or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to disaggregate applicants and awardees in Tables 1–3; counts reported for ESIs in FYs 2021–2025 (e.g., NIH supported 1,423 and 1,144 ESIs in FYs 2024 and 2025, respectively).

rubrics_metrics.name: New, non-ESI definition
rubrics_metrics.description: New, non-ESI are new to the NIH system but more than 10 years beyond their terminal degree or completion of clinical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a distinct career-stage category in Tables 1–3 when reporting applicants, discussed applications, awardees, and rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: At-Risk Investigator definition
rubrics_metrics.description: At-Risk Investigators are those who have received a prior substantial NIH award but will have no funding the following fiscal year if they are not successful in securing a competing award this year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported separately in Tables 1–3 to capture investigators whose continuation in the research workforce may be jeopardized if not re-funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established investigator definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators have received a prior substantial NIH award and will have NIH funding the following fiscal year irrespective of the outcome of this year’s competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the comparator career-stage in Tables 1–3 for applicants, discussed, awardees, discussion rates, funding rates, and age statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion Rate (person-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Discussion Rate is a person-based metric that is the percent of applicants (people designated as PIs on an application) who had at least one application make it to the discussion stage of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by career stage and fiscal year in Table 2 (e.g., ESI Discussion Rate: 63.2% in 2024, 62.2% in 2025); useful for assessing probability an applicant reaches panel discussion at least once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Rate is reported by career stage and fiscal year as the percent of applicants who received an award (Awardees divided by Applicants in the tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside Discussion Rate to show disparities across career stages (e.g., ESI funding rate 26.1% in 2024 vs. 18.9% in 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age statistics by career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Median and mean ages (and counts) for applicants and awardees by career stage are reported (Table 3); e.g., median age for ESIs in FYs 2024 and 2025 was 40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant counts in Table 3 reflect only researchers who self-reported age (optional), so these counts are lower than in Tables 1 and 2; users should note self-reporting bias when interpreting age metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizing ESI applications for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH continues making considerable efforts to enhance support for ESIs such as prioritizing ESI applications for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational policy intended to increase ESI award rates; reported counts and rates should be interpreted in light of this priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separating ESI applications from established investigators during review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH separates ESI applications from established investigators during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation is intended to provide fairer comparison among similarly resourced investigators; implementation details are part of NIH peer review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing a simplified framework for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH implemented a simplified framework for peer review to create a fairer and more transparent evaluation process for emerging researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a measure to support ESIs; affects how applications are evaluated during review and possibly discussion/funding rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating ESI needs into NIH Unified Funding Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH is integrating the needs of early career investigators directly into core funding tenets as part of the recently released NIH Unified Funding Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents a higher-level policy commitment expected to shape funding priorities and program design affecting ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizing New Innovator and Katz Awards for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH is prioritizing funding for the New Innovator and Katz Awards encouraging early career researchers to pursue innovative and possibly high-risk, high-reward research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These award programs are highlighted as targeted funding mechanisms to advance early-career innovation; prioritization may affect distribution of funds to ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards are made to institutions, not individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH makes awards to institutions (not individual researchers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting investigators supported, NIH refers to investigators applying for and receiving awards, but the legal/operational awardee is an institution; this distinction matters for institutional administration and interpretation of "supported investigators."

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy requiring use of 50% of remaining competing RPG funds for full-year funded competing RPGs (June 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH implemented a requirement to use 50% of its remaining competing Research Project Grant (RPG) funds (starting in June 2025) for full-year funded competing RPGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH notes this policy was expected to lead to fewer awards and support fewer researchers overall and may help explain decreases in ESI awardees in FY 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality and correction note
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor's Note: Table 3 was edited on 2/26/26 to correct the 14,034 at-risk awards to 1,403.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates attention to data accuracy and that published tables may be corrected post-publication; users should ensure they reference the corrected figures.
